problems.title: Original-loss smoothness does not give the composite rate
claim: The lemma uses original-loss smoothness for \(\Phi(B,U)=F(BUU^T)\) and simultaneous product-manifold updates.
analysis: Use \(F(W)=W_{12}^2/2\), \(U(a)=(\cos a,\sin a)^T\), \(B_0=\operatorname{diag}(2,0)\), \(a_0=0.05\), and step \(1/2\). The original loss is globally \(1\)-smooth. For \(q=b\cos a\sin a+c\sin^2a\), in \(|b-2|<0.1,|c|<0.1,|a|<0.1\), \(\partial_aq>1.9\cos0.2-0.1\sin0.2>1\), yielding PL constant \(\mu=1\). Exact simultaneous updates give \(a_1=0.05-\sin(0.2)/2\), \(B_{1,11}=1.99750832\), \(B_{1,12}=-0.00012469\). Both endpoints remain there, yet \(\Phi_1=0.00483999>\Phi_0/2=0.00249168\).
result: The claimed rate fails despite the stated smoothness, local PL and exact manifold step; the actual step still decreases loss.
repair: Use a composite pullback descent constant on an invariant neighborhood. Its reciprocal step condition plus PL gives a geometric value bound; the composite constant need not equal the original one.
problems.impact_rationale: An admissible manifold step violates the central convergence-rate lemma.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Global coverage does not preserve local minima at folds
claim: Global surjectivity or density of rotations is claimed to preserve local minima.
analysis: Let \(C=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)\), \(F(W)=\|W-C\|_F^2/2\), \(\bar U=e_1\), and \(a(s)=\pi/4+s^2+s^3\). On \(\theta\ne0\), put \(s=\log|\theta|\), \(R(\theta)=\operatorname{Rot}(a(s))\operatorname{diag}(1,\operatorname{sgn}\theta)\). This smooth map covers \(O(2)\). Minimizing over \(B\) gives \(f(a)=1/2+(3/2)\sin^2a\). Near \(\theta=1\), \(a\ge\pi/4\), so \((C,1)\) is a joint local minimum of value \(5/4\). A smaller ambient angle lowers loss, so its image is not an ambient minimum.
result: A globally covering map can fold locally; density need not even provide an exact preimage.
repair: Require local openness, such as a submersion, for the reverse local-minimum implication and differential surjectivity for stationarity transfer.
problems.impact_rationale: The theorem asserting unchanged optimization geometry is false for a smooth covering parameterization.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Rotation Jacobian stabilizers defeat near-isometry
problems.source_location: Appendix A.1, Jacobian expansion and Corollary 1
claim: The full rotation Jacobian is claimed near-isometric at zero, preserving Hessian conditioning.
analysis: For \(d=3,r=1,\bar U=e_1\) and Frobenius-orthonormal skew generators, \[J(0)=[e_2/\sqrt2,e_3/\sqrt2,0],\qquad J(0)^TJ(0)=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1/2,0).\] The last generator fixes the frame. At quadratic optimum \(B=C=e_1e_1^T,U=e_1\), \(H_U=\operatorname{diag}(4,1,1)\) but \(J^TH_UJ=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1/2,0)\), violating the claimed positive lower comparison. The skew-exponential integral derivative also gives \(\|J(\theta)\|_2\le1\), excluding the asserted forward singular-value blow-up.
result: Near-isometry fails at the clipped center. Empirical optimizer instability is not inferred.
repair: Remove stabilizer coordinates and use a full-rank chart. For a positive definite Hessian, \(\kappa(J^THJ)\le\kappa(H)\kappa(J)^2\) is a valid conditional comparison.
problems.impact_rationale: An exact zero mode contradicts the central geometric conditioning justification.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Reduced orbits can contain an optimum and create traps
claim: The no-spurious-minimum conclusion is retained if an optimum is reachable or close to the reduced orbit.
analysis: For \(d=4,r=2,\bar U=[e_1,e_3]\), \(C=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,1,0)\), rotate the two planes at speeds \(1\) and \(2\). Minimizing \(\|BUU^T-C\|_F^2/2\) over \(B\) gives \(f(\theta)=[\sin^2\theta+\sin^2(2\theta)]/2\). The orbit has zero loss at \(0\), but at \(\pi/2\), \(f=1/2,f'=0,f''=3>0\), giving a joint restricted local minimum. Rotating only the first column toward its original axis lowers ambient loss.
result: Optimum containment does not prevent restricted-orbit traps. This witness lies outside practical clipping radius \(0.5\), so it does not establish a trapped clipped run.
repair: Restrict the landscape statement to the orbit or require all relevant ambient descent directions to be represented.
problems.impact_rationale: The broad reduced-family landscape guarantee fails even with exact optimum containment.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Stochastic decay is an expected bound, not pathwise pruning
claim: The proof reverses the norm/expectation comparison, while the main discussion suggests a pathwise limit.
analysis: Let \(P\) be either coordinate projector equally likely, \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,0),\lambda=1,\eta=1/2\), and bounded smooth \(F_x(Z)=3-h(Z_{11})\), where \(h(t)=t\) on \([-2,2]\), \(|h'|\le1,|h|\le5/2\). From zero, \(W_t=w_tQ\) obeys \(w_{t+1}=w_t/2+\xi_t/2\), with independent Bernoulli halves. Thus \(Ew_t=(1-2^{-t})/2\), but arbitrarily long all-one/all-zero blocks give almost surely \(\limsup w_t=1,\liminf w_t=0\).
result: The stronger pathwise reading fails; the formal expected bound survives a corrected proof. Derivatives through trainable projectors remain a separate condition.
repair: Take triangle inequality before expectation to obtain \(y_{t+1}\le(1-\eta\lambda)y_t+\eta Lp_Q\), sum the geometric series, and state an expected limsup.
problems.impact_rationale: The formal stochastic theorem remains recoverable; this is a local proof and interpretation defect.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Average overlap alone does not justify projection removal
claim: Weight decay is used to infer redundancy of sample-dependent projections.
analysis: Let coordinate projectors \(P_1,P_2\) be equally likely, \(F_i(Z)=1-e^{-\|Z-P_i\|_F^2}\), and \(\lambda=e^{-1/4}\). Gradients are globally bounded by \(\sqrt{2/e}<1\). The regularized objective has Hessian lower bound \((e^{-1/4}-2e^{-3/2})I\succ0\) and zero gradient at \(W_*=I/2\), hence this is its unique optimum. For each sample, removal changes loss from \(1-e^{-1/4}\) to \(1-e^{-1/2}\), an increase \(0.17227012\). No globally idle direction exists.
result: The overlap theorem lacks samplewise residual control even at an optimum. The reported removal/fine-tuning experiment remains separate empirical evidence.
repair: Expected residual \(E\|XW(I-P(x))\|_F\le\varepsilon\) and downstream Lipschitz constant \(K\) suffice for expected loss change at most \(K\varepsilon\); the overlap bound does not establish this premise.
problems.impact_rationale: The theoretical removal bridge is incomplete, without disproving empirical paired removal results.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.
